title: Inertia startup relaxation and normalized frequency-mass scaling
description: Mathematical consequences of a first-order relaxation equation and the Planck-Einstein energy mass equivalent. The algebra is DER under its stated assumptions; it does not establish that a particular physical system follows the relaxation model.
definitions: X(t) is a quantity with the same units as its asymptotic value X_max.
X_max is constant and is the long-time limit of X(t).
t is elapsed time, and tau is a positive characteristic time with the same unit as t.
m(f) is the inertial mass equivalent of energy h f, not photon rest mass or the rest mass of an arbitrary oscillator.
f and f_0 are positive ordinary frequencies measured in the same frame; f_0 = 8 Hz.
equations: For X(0) = 0, separation and integration give X(t) = X_max * (1 - exp(-t/tau))
The exponent t/tau is dimensionless; for general X(0) = X_i, X(t) = X_max + (X_i - X_max) * exp(-t/tau)
assumptions: The relaxation equation has constant X_max and tau over the interval considered.
The stated zero-initial-value curve assumes X(0) = 0; the more general solution uses the separately specified initial value X_i.
h is the Planck constant, c is the vacuum speed of light, and E = h f is the energy of the frequency quantum.
The ratio f/f_0 is dimensionless because both frequencies use the same units; f_0 = 8 Hz is a reference frequency, not a dimensional multiplier applied directly to mass.
The factor 162 is treated as a dimensionless model constant; v_tilde must be dimensionless and nonzero for Psi_norm to be defined.
The norm ||v||_E8 denotes a declared E8-space norm with the same velocity units as c; no physical E8 velocity space is inferred by this notation.
mechanism: The relaxation curve is obtained by solving the declared linear ordinary differential equation. The mass scaling follows by substituting m_0 = h f_0/c^2 and cancelling the common reference frequency. Psi_norm is dimensionless because h f and m c^2 are both energies, while 162/v_tilde is dimensionless.
primary_sources: SI Brochure, 9th edition: definitions and units of the second, hertz, Planck constant h, and speed of light c
Einstein, 1905, Does the Inertia of a Body Depend Upon Its Energy? (mass-energy equivalence)
predictions: For fixed positive tau and X(0) = 0, the model has X(0) = 0 and approaches X_max as t/tau increases.
For positive f and f_0 = 8 Hz, m(f)/m_0 = f/f_0 and m(f) has units kg.
If m is set equal to h f/c^2, then h f/(m c^2) = 1 and Psi_norm reduces to 162/v_tilde when v_tilde is nonzero.
falsification_conditions: Differentiating the stated solution does not recover dX/dt = (X_max - X)/tau under the declared constant-parameter assumptions.
The exponent t/tau is not dimensionless for the declared time units.
Algebraic substitution with common h, c, f and f_0 does not yield m(f) = h f/c^2 or units of kg.
A claimed numerical value of Psi_norm is undefined because m = 0 or v_tilde = 0, or because its declared inputs do not make the expression dimensionless.
confusion_guard: A valid derivation establishes algebra conditional on the stated model; it does not establish a measured relaxation process, a physical E8 velocity space, or an empirical interpretation of the factor 162.
